transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I just... I really didn't know what else to do at this point, to be honest. I'm here because for a long time now—and I mean a really, really long time—my sleep has just been completely broken. 

I mean, with my job, I'm a home health aide, so I'm constantly moving, helping people, lifting them, and by the end of my shift I am just totally wiped out. I fall into bed absolutely exhausted, like my whole body just aches for sleep and I can barely keep my eyes open. But then... I don't know, it's like my body just won't stay under. I wake up to every little sound in the house. If the refrigerator kicks on, or if the floorboards settle, or even just the wind outside, my eyes just snap open. 

And once I'm awake, I just toss and turn. I'll look at the clock and it's 3:00 or 4:00 in the morning, and then I'm just up way before my alarm even goes off. I'll just lie there staring at the ceiling in the dark, knowing I have to go to work soon, and when it is finally time to get up, I feel like I never really rested at all. It's like I was just hovering awake the whole night, and I'm just running on fumes every single day. It's just been going on for so many months that I just... I don't know how to fix it, and I'm just so tired all the time...
Have you noticed that your mood has been low or that you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well, yes... honestly, "low" almost sounds too simple for it. It’s more like... I don't know, most days I feel like all the color has just completely gone out of things. Like everything is just washed out and gray. 

I’ll be sitting right there at Sunday dinner with my family—and we always do a big Sunday dinner, my sister usually cooks, the whole family is there laughing and passing food around—and I’m physically there, but I just feel so disconnected from it all. Or even with things just for me... I used to really enjoy looking at art, you know, going to little local shows or just admiring pieces that had so much life and vibrancy to them. It used to bring me a lot of joy. Now I look at them and it’s just... flat. I look at the canvas and I feel absolutely nothing at all. 

And the hardest part is, while I'm sitting there at the dinner table with everyone, or just going about my day, I have to work so, so hard not to just tear up. Out of nowhere, I'll get this huge lump in my throat and feel like I'm about to start crying for absolutely no clear reason. There’s no trigger, nothing sad even happened, someone could just be telling a story about their week, but I have to bite the inside of my cheek or excuse myself to the bathroom so my family doesn't see me fall apart. It’s just this constant, heavy sadness that I drag around with me everywhere, and it just makes everything feel so hollow, you know? Like I'm just going through the motions of being a person but I can't actually feel any of the good parts anymore, no matter how hard I try to force a smile...
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or feel fatigued most of the time, even when you haven't done much physically?

Oh, absolutely. I mean, it's just a constant, overwhelming feeling of being drained, and it's not just the normal kind of tired you get after a long day. Like I mentioned, I work as a home health aide, and I know that's a physical job. I'm helping people in and out of bed, assisting them with bathing, sometimes doing light housekeeping for them because they just can't do it themselves anymore. And I've been doing this for a long time, so I know what it feels like to have a physically demanding day. 

But this... this is different. It's like my bones are made of lead. By the time I finish seeing my clients for the day and I finally walk through my own front door, my body just feels so incredibly heavy. And it's not even just the physical stuff that wipes me out. I have to do my charting, you know, writing down the notes for each client, tracking their vitals, making sure I document everything for the agency. It used to take me maybe twenty minutes to get through it all. Now? Now I'll just sit down at the kitchen table with my laptop, and just the thought of typing out those notes feels like I'm trying to push a boulder up a hill. 

And then there's the stuff around the house. My sister does a lot, especially with the Sunday dinners, but I still try to help out where I can, you know? But lately, even something as simple as folding a basket of laundry... I'll pull the clothes out of the dryer, and they're warm, and I'll put the basket on the bed, and I just stare at it. Picking up a towel and folding it in half just feels like it requires more energy than I have in my entire body. I just don't have the strength to push through it anymore. It's like my battery is constantly at one percent, no matter what I'm doing or how little I've actually done that day. I just feel so weighed down by it all, and it makes every single little task feel like a monumental chore that I just can't manage.
Have you found yourself feeling overly guilty about things, or like you’re not good enough, even when there’s no real reason for it?

No, I... I don't really think so. I mean, I don't feel guilty about things, not really. I know I do a good job with my clients. Like Mrs. Higgins, she's one of my regulars, and she always tells me I'm the only one who gets her pillows fluffed exactly right, and I make sure her tea is just the way she likes it before I leave. I know I'm good at my job, and I know I care about the people I help. 

And my family, well, I know they love me and I love them. I don't feel like I'm a burden or anything like that, or like I'm doing something wrong. I mean, my sister is always telling me not to worry about helping with the Sunday dinners lately because she knows how tired I am, and she doesn't make me feel bad about it at all. It's not a feeling of being a bad person or feeling worthless... it's just this incredible, overwhelming emptiness and exhaustion. I just feel so drained, like I was saying before, with the laundry and the charting. But no, I don't sit around feeling guilty or like I'm not good enough. I just feel... tired. Just so, so tired and gray.
